rules.reason: broomrape (canavar otu, Orobanche cumana) seeds stay viable for years; damage was highest in the 2-year wheat-sunflower rotation
rules.source: Shevchenko 2024, Sunflower broomrape (Orobanche cumana Wallr.), Dnipro State Agrarian and Economic University

rules.reason: beet cyst nematode (Heterodera schachtii) needs 3-4 years of non-host crops to decline, more in heavily infested fields
rules.source: Journal of Nematology 2024, rate of decline of sugarbeet cyst nematode under nonhost crops; University of Nebraska bulletin as cited there

rules.reason: Ascochyta blight (antraknoz) survives on chickpea residue for several years
rules.source: NDSU Extension, Ascochyta blight of chickpea: fundamentals of management (minimum 3-year rotation); Agriculture and Agri-Food Canada (3-4 years)

rules.reason: Ascochyta and other residue-borne diseases of lentil: at least two non-host crops between lentil crops
rules.source: USDA ARS, General principles for managing chickpea and lentil diseases (compendium part 5)

rules.reason: soilborne diseases (black scurf, common scab, Verticillium) build up; 2-year rotations did not prevent increases
rules.source: Larkin et al. review of potato soilborne disease and rotation (PMC); Idaho potato advice cited by Bayer Crop Science (minimum 3 years)

rules.reason: blackleg increased when canola was grown more than once in four years
rules.source: Canadian Journal of Plant Pathology 2013, effects of canola rotation frequency on blackleg (one canola crop in 4 years)

rules.reason: take-all and other cereal root diseases are worst in second and later wheats; a one-year non-cereal break mostly prevents it
rules.source: Rothamsted Research (Annals of Applied Biology, aab.12139); Oregon State University Extension EC 1423

rules.reason: potato and tomato share soilborne diseases and pests; growing one after the other gives them no break
rules.source: compiled rule (shared hosts of soilborne potato diseases; see the potato review above); needs expert check

rules.reason: a legume before a cereal raised the next crop's yield by about 20% on average (462 studies, 53 countries)
rules.source: Zhao et al. 2022, Nature Communications 13:4926, yield advantage of legume-based rotations

rules.reason: brassicas such as canola before potato reduced Rhizoctonia disease in Canadian research
rules.source: Agriculture and Agri-Food Canada research (R. Peters) reported by Top Crop Manager, rotational options being studied
